## App and account limits
The following limits apply for creating legacy apps, webhook subscriptions, and CRM extension settings.
- You can create up to 100 [legacy public apps](/docs/apps/legacy-apps/public-apps/overview) per developer account.
- You can create up to 20 [legacy private apps](/docs/apps/legacy-apps/private-apps/overview) per HubSpot account.
- You can create up to 1,000 [webhook subscriptions](/docs/api-reference/latest/webhooks) per app.
- You can create up to 25 CRM extension settings per [legacy public app](/docs/apps/legacy-apps/public-apps/overview).

No. You can create a free HubSpot account and build apps without a paid subscription. You'll get access to a developer test account with sample data for testing. For production deployments, your app's users will need appropriate HubSpot accounts.
###
A free developer account includes:
- **Test accounts** with sample CRM data (contacts, companies, deals) for development and testing
- **API access** to HubSpot’s public APIs for development and testing
- **App management** to create, configure, and publish apps
- **CLI access** to create and deploy Projects
- **AI-native developer documentation**
Test accounts reset periodically but are fully functional for building and testing your integrations.
###
When you convert your developer portal, you get **2 Super Admin core seats** with full access to CRM and development tools. Additional users can be added as **developer seats** which provide access to development tools without using a paid CRM seat.
Developer seats let your team collaborate on apps without requiring paid HubSpot subscriptions.

title: HubSpot API: what to build and the limits | Längle Digital
snippet:
The HubSpot API lets your other systems read and write HubSpot data, and lets HubSpot tell them when something changes. Every HubSpot plan has it, including the free CRM, and API calls cost no extra fee. What your plan decides is how many calls you get, which objects you can reach and whether workflows can run code.

AccessA service key for simple data jobs, an app built as a HubSpot project for webhooks or cards. New legacy private apps can’t be created after 26 October 2026
Limits190 calls per 10 seconds on Professional and Enterprise. 625,000 calls a day on Professional, 1,000,000 on Enterprise, 250,000 on Free and Starter
BatchUp to 100 records per call, so a daily limit covers millions of record changes
EditionsCRM data on every plan. Custom objects Enterprise. Code and webhooks inside workflows need Data Hub Professional
VersionsDated versions since March 2026, now 2026-09. v4 unsupported from 30 March 2027, v1 to v3 and legacy apps from September 2027
OwnerEvery integration needs a named person who reads its error log and HubSpot’s developer changelog

The API is a set of web addresses at api.hubapi.com, one family per object, with the data as JSON. A developer needs an access key with the right permissions (HubSpot calls them scopes), the documentation at developers.hubspot.com and a test account. HubSpot gives developers free test accounts with a 90-day trial of many Enterprise features.

| Access | Use it for | Can do | Can’t do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service key | An internal sync, a script or a tool like Make on your own account | API calls with the scopes you tick, a call log, rotation with seven days’ overlap | Webhooks, cards or anything beyond API calls. Public beta as of October 2026 |
| App built as a HubSpot project, static token | Your own integration in one account that also needs webhooks or a card | API calls, webhooks, app cards and pages, workflow actions | Install in more than one standard account |
| App built as a HubSpot project, OAuth | An integration you install in several accounts or list in the marketplace | Everything above, per installing account | Run without a server that handles the OAuth sign-in |
| Legacy private app | Existing integrations only | Keeps working for now | New ones can’t be created after 26 October 2026; support ends September 2027 |

title: HubSpot API review: limits, auth and what is free
snippet:
# 250,000 calls a day, shared across every app
```
200 OK Per call, any plan $0.00
The HubSpot API is the one record in this directory where the interesting number is not a price. CRM reads and writes are not metered, the free tier includes API access rather than just the web app, and a pipeline that creates ten thousand contacts a month pays the same as one that creates ten.
What you are buying is throughput. Every call counts against two windows, and both are set by the product tier of the account the app is installed in: 100 requests per 10 seconds on Free and Starter, 190 on Professional and Enterprise, with a daily ceiling of 250,000, 625,000 and 1,000,000 respectively. The burst window is per app. The daily one is shared across every app in the account, which is the part that catches teams out.

There is no line item called the HubSpot API. Access comes with the plan, and the plan sets your limits, so the HubSpot API cost for most GTM pipelines is zero and the real question is which tier buys enough headroom.

title: Is the HubSpot API free?
snippet:
Yes, the HubSpot API is free to use: HubSpot doesn't charge per API call, and every account, including free ones, gets API access within documented limits. What you pay for is indirect. Daily limits rise with your subscription tier, a paid API limit increase raises them further, and some endpoints only work if your account has the feature, such as workflows.
On this page
## What HubSpot supports natively
HubSpot doesn’t sell API access separately. Your subscription decides how much you can call, not whether you can (limits for privately distributed apps, checked October 29, 2026):
| Subscription | Burst limit | Daily limit (per account) |
|---|---|---|
| Free and Starter | 100 requests per 10 seconds, per app | 250,000 |
| Professional | 190 per 10 seconds, per app | 625,000 |
| Enterprise | 190 per 10 seconds, per app | 1,000,000 |
| With an API limit increase | 250 per 10 seconds, per app | +1,000,000 per increase (maximum two) |
Apps listed on the HubSpot Marketplace and installed with OAuth have a separate limit of 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account, which the API limit increase doesn’t raise. HubSpot points to its Product & Services Catalog for the increase’s price.
## Where the API isn’t free in practice
- **Feature-gated endpoints.** The API can only do what the account can. If the portal doesn’t have workflows, or HubDB, the scope and the endpoint aren’t available. Scopes depend on what the account includes.
- **Heavy integrations.** A sync that outgrows 250,000 calls a day on Starter pushes you toward a higher tier or the limit increase.
- **Developer time.** Retries, paging and error handling are the real cost of most integrations. HubSpot asks that errors stay under 5% of your daily requests.
## How to keep HubSpot API usage free
1. **Use batch endpoints** instead of one call per record.
2. **Use search for filtered reads**, but note it has its own limit of 5 requests per second per account.
3. **Cache what doesn’t change**, such as property definitions and pipelines.
4. **Watch the headers.** `X-HubSpot-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining` tells you how much of today’s allowance is left.
5. **Test in a free developer test account**, not in production.
